sections.heading: Hegota EIP Tier List and ZK-Relevant EIPs
sections.summary: EF published a Hegota tier list; EIP-8025 rated A-ish, EVMification EIP rated C, and BlockHash-via-storage EIP is capacity-dependent.
sections.body:
- The EF published a blog post with a tier list for Hegota, rating EIPs across protocol cluster teams (client teams, research, engineering) ([ignacio's slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1hVTqWOu5glMIbyNLcLi7W1I7O_1DlZFv6e-lDsWJndE/edit?usp=sharing)).
- EIP-8025 received an A-ish score; the main argument is upstreaming the execution specs branch that defines what the stateless guest program should do.
  - The branch is zkVM-agnostic and fully defines stateless block execution and required checks.
  - It does not change the state transition function; it is invasive only in testing framework internals (new fields like stateless input bytes, stateless output bytes, and transition tool support).
- The EVMification EIP (championed by Kev) received a C rating.
  - It transforms rarely-used precompiles into EVM bytecode, enabling more natural repricing for zkVMs.
  - Challenges include formally verifying bytecode transformations, deciding whether EL clients run the bytecodes, and gas cost implications.
- The BlockHash EIP (championed by ignacio) would resolve BLOCKHASH via EIP-2935 storage, simplifying stateless input by removing a dedicated field.
  - Inclusion depends on available capacity in Hegota.
  - There is a UX impact analysis available regarding the indirect repricing (now SLOAD instead of dedicated opcode).

sections.heading: EIP-8025 Repository and Documentation
sections.summary: A new EIP-8025 repository provides an argument document, Q&A, and engineering progress page to clarify the proposal for core devs.
sections.body:
- A new repository called EIP-8025 has been created and shared with EL and CL core devs via DM.
- The repo contains an ACD.md file that precisely argues why EIP-8025 should be included in Hegota, addressing confusion about 8025 vs. mandatory proofs.
- An ACD Q&A section collects previously received questions with answers, plus anticipated important questions.
- A progress.md file serves as an engineering landing page for zkVM progress on L1, covering CL branches, tooling descriptions, all breakout call slides, and related links.
  - Intended to be maintained as a single source of truth, also useful as LLM context.

sections.heading: Specs, Tests, and Benchmark Releases
sections.summary: Test zkVM spec releases reached v0.8x with simplified stateless input; first official benchmark fixtures released for 10M, 30M, and 60M gas.
sections.body:
- Version 0.8x of the test zkVM specs has been released, simplifying stateless input regarding chain config.
- A working method for filling EEST fixtures with an external transition tool (currently Geth) has been established.
- First official test zkVM benchmark release provides benchmark fixtures for 10M, 30M, and 60M gas.
  - Future releases will keep test fixtures and benchmark fixtures as separate release tracks, both from the execution-specs repository.
- Ethrex can now also fill these fixtures; choice of filler client depends on which client is up-to-date with specs.
- A new R2 bucket provides stateless input for Glamsterdam devnet 8.
  - Warning: a recent consensus-breaking spec change may cause the R2 bucket to be reset once all ELs adopt the new spec, to avoid mixing pre- and post-change blocks.

sections.heading: Guest Program DoS Vector via HashMap Randomness
sections.summary: Lukasz from Nethermind raised a potential DoS vector in guest programs due to lack of randomness seeds; a new precompile proposal is under discussion.
sections.body:
- Guest programs are pure functions with no random precompile in zkVMs, creating a challenge for data structures (e.g., HashMaps) that need randomness for uniform key distribution.
- With FOCIL, block construction is not fully controlled by the block builder, opening a potential attack vector where an attacker could bias guest programs toward worst-case scenarios.
- An issue thread is open for exploring options; Cody has created a potential new precompile proposal.
- The discussion is fresh and community input is welcome on the issue thread.

sections.heading: Tooling and Guest Program CI Improvements
sections.summary: All guest programs (ethrex, Reth, Besu) now release ELFs independently via CI, simplifying era-guests integration to a JSON config edit.
sections.body:
- Tooling repos are being updated to the latest test zkVM release, incorporating the last-minute spec change for devnet 8.
- Era-guests has fully switched to pulling ELFs directly from guest team releases.
  - Previously ethrex and Reth were compiled inside era-guests, which was undesirable since teams should own their own ELF releases.
  - Both ethrex and Reth now have CI pipelines for releases, matching Besu's original approach.
- Adding a new guest program now requires only editing a JSON file pointing to a team's release; tests (EEST fixtures, soundness checks) run automatically.

sections.heading: Proving Infrastructure Benchmarks and Cost Analysis
sections.summary: Han presented new benchmarks on OpenVM v2.1 and zkV1.2 with per-proof metrics scraping, pipeline traces, and cost estimation tooling across all three zkVMs.
sections.body:
- Benchmarks run on new test suites with OpenVM v2.1 and zkV1.2, results available in the prover benchmarker ([slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Lb6cGfTOhms_CZN4lHSnT4UAOUIlh8XZTvnAyEP6ohc/edit?slide=id.g3c598feeaac_0_0#slide=id.g3c598feeaac_0_0)).
- The benchmarker now scrapes metrics from node exporter and DC2N exporter during each proof, providing per-proof GPU utilization and phase-level detail.
- A proving pipeline trace is collected during each proof, showing idle periods and cost composition.
- Cost analysis added to the benchmarker front-end: all three zkVMs now have cost estimation tools.
  - Given a guest and input, cost can be estimated without actual proving.
  - Front-end shows cost composition, cost by category, correlation with proving time, and outlier detection.
- Ignacio noted this work will eventually link with the EVM gas repo (a tool by Maria used in Amsterdam for repricing), likely using proving times rather than cost estimation.
- Open question remains whether to standardize cost estimation or rely on proving times directly.

sections.heading: Chetany's Proving Observability Internship (EthPandaOps)
sections.summary: A 72-hour unattended mainnet proving run on 16 RTX 5090s achieved 99.4% of blocks proved within 12 seconds using OpenVM v2.0 and Axiom Edge.
sections.body:
- Chetany built "Professor," a tool that follows the standard Beacon API and sends proof requests through zkBoost (proof coordinator) ([slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1KeoK6fpf8L82XzqRXaZELPYrPZcoO4SOPmoMJtp9YKc/edit?usp=sharing)).
  - Does not require a specialized consensus client fork; uses SQLite for per-proof history; reconciles pending proofs after disconnection; exposes state timings with trace links.
  - Improvements made to zkBoost: separate witness fetch/queue weight and proving times, trace context carried across services.
- A cancellation race bug left proving workers stuck for 21.5 hours with no error logging; after fix, same failure class recovered in 72 seconds.
- Strongest run configuration: 16 RTX 5090s across 4 machines (4 GPUs each), OpenVM v2.0, first version of Axiom Edge.
  - Ran unattended ~72 hours against mainnet.
  - 99.4% of blocks proved within 12-second budget (slot time).
  - Median end-to-end latency: 6.26 seconds; P99: 11.15 seconds.
  - End-to-end measured from block observation on gossip to proof resolution; excludes gossiping/signing.
  - 5 failures: 3 witness timeouts, 2 proof fetch errors (2 during Beacon API outage).
- Witness delivery identified as biggest remaining constraint.
  - Witness fetching explained 63% of the increase from median to P99 end-to-end latency.
  - Witness generation used the old debug method, not the new SSZ method.
  - Worst-case witness fetches reached 9–11 seconds.
- Proposed next steps: closing coverage gaps with more resilient recovery, improved witness delivery with endpoint failover, deeper live-run analysis correlating blocks with proof IDs and worker phases.
- Discussion on network latency: negligible on local 10 Gbps LAN (confirmed by Yi Sun's experience with <100ms), but potentially significant with distributed/cross-network setups.
  - Orchestrator-to-worker latency matters more than worker-to-worker since workers don't communicate directly.
  - Primitive load balancing (lowest-index-first) caused uneven workload distribution; more sophisticated scheduling could help.
- Francesco asked about serialization overhead; Chetany noted Beacon API involves serialize/deserialize cycles but these are currently negligible compared to witness fetch latency.

sections.heading: Consensus Layer Spec Updates and Lighthouse Implementation
sections.summary: CL specs refactored to use execution-proof envelope keyed on beacon block root; gossip validation now includes proof verification to prevent spam.
sections.body:
- Consensus specs have been refactored around a new `execution-proof envelope` type sent over the wire; Francesco said the relevant PRs are linked in his slides, which he would share after the call.
  - Proof data and proof type remain the same, but keying changed from new payload request root to beacon block root for simpler integration.
- P2P gossip validation change: proof engine verification now happens inside the gossip handler.
  - Rationale: many validators can produce execution proofs (unlike blocks with one proposer), so signature-only gating would allow spam of invalid proofs.
  - Adds ~80ms verification latency to gossip; more benchmarking needed.
  - For mandatory proofs (one producer per slot), can revert to signature-only verification before gossiping.
- Erasure-coded broadcast work for execution payloads may also be adopted for execution proof dissemination.
- Specs merged into master.
- Francesco working on Lighthouse implementation in the EF ACT Lighthouse repository.
  - PR aligning data model to execution-proof envelope; wrapper around Han's C bindings for zkVM verifiers.
  - Intent to upstream or coordinate with Lighthouse devs on preferred approach.
  - Goal: join devnet 8 or a subsequent devnet with Gloas.
- To reduce burden on CL client teams: only proof verification support is mandatory; proof generation support is optional.
  - Tau team will support proof generation in their Lighthouse fork.
  - One client supporting proof generation is sufficient; two would be ideal; volunteer client teams welcome.

sections.heading: Professor Live Demo
sections.summary: Chetany demoed Professor running on a local Kurtosis devnet, showing per-proof tracing, reconciliation, and Grafana/Tempo integration.
sections.body:
- Professor demonstrated on a local Kurtosis devnet with two zkBoost instances (Rust node and SP1) and two Professor nodes.
- UI shows live blocks, cadence metrics (min/max turnaround, failure count), filtering by status (failed, completed, in-flight), and sorting.
- Per-proof detail includes witness generation time, throughput time, and generation time; clicking a trace ID links to Tempo/Grafana for exact time breakdown.
  - Shows time for block fetch, request build, zkBoost submission, and where visibility ends (zkVM coordinators don't expose internal pipeline).
- Reconciliation demonstrated: if Professor disconnects and restarts, it reconciles missed proofs that were submitted but not completed.
  - Does not reconcile blocks missed entirely (old proofs not helpful), but recovers submitted requests.
- Kurtosis Ethereum package integration not yet publicly merged; debugging needed around blob increase and PBOs before release.
